requirements.requirement: The system must return a relevance_score of 1.0 for exact condition matches between user input and trial conditions.
The system must return a relevance_score greater than 0 and less than 1.0 for partial matches between user input and trial conditions.
The system must return a relevance_score of 0.0 when no match is found between user input and trial conditions.
The system must correctly handle multiple user conditions and return the highest applicable relevance_score.
The system must return a structured response including relevance_score, match_type, and matched_terms for all test cases.
The system must propagate the computed relevance_score through the evaluation facade without alteration.
The system must include an integration test verifying that condition relevance results are present in the facade API response.
The system must normalize condition inputs (case, spacing, synonyms) consistently before matching in all test scenarios.
The system must handle null or empty user condition input by returning a relevance_score of 0.0 and match_type indicating no_input.
The system must handle null or empty trial conditions by returning a relevance_score of 0.0 without throwing an error.
The system must produce deterministic relevance_score outputs for identical inputs across repeated test runs.
The system must ensure semantic similarity fallback produces a non-zero relevance_score when synonym conditions are used (e.g., 'heart attack' vs 'myocardial infarction').
The system must ensure LLM-based or semantic matching does not exceed a relevance_score of 1.0 under any condition.
The system must validate that match_type values returned are restricted to defined enum values (exact, partial, semantic, none, no_input).
The system must include test coverage for at least two exception paths: null user input and null trial conditions, both completing without runtime errors.
